hook: Soumith Chintala spent eleven years at Facebook and Meta building the infrastructure researchers actually use, and in 2016 that work became PyTorch, a framework Meta's own engineering blog credits him with co-creating. PyTorch went from a research tool to the default choice for training large language models and most of the vision and generative models that followed it. In January 2026 he left the company where he built his career to become Chief Technology Officer at Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab, taking on AI infrastructure and research at a new frontier lab. He also holds an affiliation at NYU, the university where he earned his master's degree under Yann LeCun, working there on home robotics with Lerrel Pinto.

standing.watch: What the records leave open is mostly on the Meta side of the ledger. In Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc., summary judgment was granted for Meta on fair use in June 2025, and plaintiffs are seeking interlocutory appeal certification as of August 25, 2026, so that question is not closed. In State of New Mexico ex rel. Torrez v. Meta Platforms, Inc., the jury found Facebook liable for deceiving users about privacy protections with more than 43 million violations of the New Mexico Unfair Practices Act, and penalties are to be set at a hearing on October 1, 2026, with the state seeking up to $5,000 per violation; claims that Facebook misrepresented removal of harmful content were rejected. Neural AI, LLC v. Meta Platforms, Inc. and Chicken Soup for the Soul, LLC v. Meta Platforms Inc. remain filed with no development recorded by this tracker. On Chintala himself the records show only the January 2026 move to Thinking Machines Lab and the continuing NYU robotics affiliation, with nothing further recorded about either.
standing.record: The site's company records place Chintala at Meta, as an executive of the public company founded in 2004 in Menlo Park, and as a founder of Meta / Linux Foundation. His technical record in the same file is the co-creation of PyTorch and co-authorship of early generative adversarial network papers including DCGAN and Wasserstein GAN, alongside a bachelor's degree from VIT Vellore and a master's in computer science from NYU. The lawsuits on the site all name Meta Platforms, not Chintala: Neural AI, LLC v. Meta Platforms, Inc. and Chicken Soup for the Soul, LLC v. Meta Platforms Inc. are both recorded as filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet. Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc. ended in summary judgment for Meta on fair use in June 2025, and the State of New Mexico ex rel. Torrez v. Meta Platforms, Inc. produced a jury verdict for the state on September 25, 2026. The pattern is that the coverage and the litigation attach to the company he spent eleven years inside, while the record of him personally is a framework and a set of research papers.
standing.standing: Soumith Chintala is Chief Technology Officer at Thinking Machines Lab, a position the records show he has held since January 2026, after leaving Meta in 2025. His standing rests on PyTorch, which Meta's own engineering blog credits him with co-creating and which was released as open source in January 2017, and which the profile describes as having become the default choice for training large language models and most of the vision and generative models that followed. Before the move he rose to Vice President of Engineering over an eleven-year career at Facebook and Meta, so his influence runs through infrastructure that other researchers use rather than through a product he owns. He also holds an affiliation at NYU, where he earned a master's degree under Yann LeCun and works on home robotics with Lerrel Pinto. The site lists him as an executive of Meta and as a founder of Meta / Linux Foundation, and lists no company of his own beyond those entries.

timeline.event: Earns a bachelor's degree from VIT Vellore in India
timeline.impact: Starting point of his technical education, after applying to and being rejected by numerous US graduate programs

timeline.event: Joins Facebook AI Research as a research engineer
timeline.impact: Begins an eleven-year run building AI research and production infrastructure at the company

timeline.event: Co-creates PyTorch within Facebook AI Research
timeline.impact: Lays the groundwork for what Meta's engineering blog calls the preferred deep learning library for AI researchers

timeline.event: PyTorch is released publicly as open-source software
timeline.impact: Puts the framework directly into the hands of the broader research community

timeline.event: Departs Meta after eleven years, having risen to Vice President of Engineering
timeline.impact: Closes out more than a decade leading one of the most widely used pieces of AI infrastructure

timeline.event: Appointed Chief Technology Officer of Thinking Machines Lab in January
timeline.impact: Takes on infrastructure and research leadership at a new frontier AI lab

quick_facts: Chief Technology Officer at Thinking Machines Lab since January 2026
Co-created PyTorch at Facebook AI Research, released as open source in January 2017
Rose to Vice President of Engineering at Meta over an eleven-year career there before departing in 2025
Holds a bachelor's degree from VIT Vellore and a master's in computer science from NYU, where he studied under Yann LeCun
Affiliated with NYU, working on home robotics with Lerrel Pinto
Co-authored early generative adversarial network papers including DCGAN and Wasserstein GAN

achievements.title: Co-created PyTorch
achievements.impact: Built, with a Facebook AI Research team, the open-source deep learning framework that Meta's own engineering blog says became the preferred library for AI researchers and now underlies most modern large language and vision model training.

achievements.title: Led PyTorch for nearly a decade
achievements.impact: Continued to lead the PyTorch team inside Meta as it grew from a research project into the framework migrated across Meta's production AI stack, with PyTorch 1.0 merging it with the production-oriented Caffe2 in 2018.

achievements.title: Chief Technology Officer, Thinking Machines Lab
achievements.impact: Took on AI infrastructure, research, and technical direction at a frontier AI lab founded by former OpenAI Chief Technology Officer Mira Murati.

achievements.title: convnet-benchmarks
achievements.impact: Built an open-source deep learning hardware and software benchmark suite that NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel referenced when comparing training performance.
